rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first oath's unstated complement is self-evident; Qāf and Ṣād likewise omit their oath complements, as what deniers reject itself testifies to truth.
rows.anchor: the oath itself bears evidence to its complement.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second oath's omitted complement is implicit: the reproaching soul itself evidences the Day of Judgement, so no external proof is needed.
rows.anchor: no external evidence is required for that Day.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reproaching soul is part of the human soul, whose God-given awareness of good and evil makes purification succeed and corruption fail.
rows.anchor: The reproaching soul is not an independent entity; it is part of the human soul.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inspires the soul with good and evil; a person succeeds by purifying it and fails by corrupting it.
rows.anchor: then [God] inspired it with its evil and its good that he succeeded who purified it and he failed who soiled it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When desire overcomes the soul and prompts evil, this tendency is the Qur’an’s Enticing Soul; Joseph describes the soul as prone to evil.
rows.anchor: The Prophet Joseph (sws) has referred to this aspect of the soul thus

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reproaching soul is the soul's virtuous awareness: when balanced, it reproaches its own wrongdoing and condemns vice in others.
rows.anchor: It is this aspect of the soul which is called the reproaching soul here.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God and the Judgement checks desire; after an error, the soul exposes the folly and turns a person toward repentance and repair.
rows.anchor: keep his Lord and the Day of Judgement in his remembrance. This remembrance checks the soul

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The balanced, disciplined soul is the highest human state; God grants divine law to help people attain it and will be pleased with that soul.
rows.anchor: The Almighty has urged him to try to attain this position

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cain's concealment after killing Abel shows innate awareness of sin; people act from overpowering desire, yet recognize the same vice when others commit it against them.
rows.anchor: he tried to hide his corpse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Societies retain a collective conscience that condemns vice and have people who serve as the community's reproaching soul, even when sin dominates.
rows.anchor: the collective conscience of the society never condones this.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A society wholly bereft of virtue is, under providence, wiped from the earth.
rows.anchor: as per the law of providence, such a society is wiped out from the face of the earth.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conscience is God's miniature court: its pain at wrongdoing implies that people will face a greater judgement for good and evil and receive recompense.
rows.anchor: Any person who deliberates on these questions while disregarding his desires will reach the conclusion that the very being of a person bears witness

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sages call man a miniature world reflecting the greater world; true self-knowledge leads to knowledge of God and the Hereafter, echoing Socrates' “Know Thyself.”
rows.anchor: man is a miniature world

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although phrased universally, “man” addresses Quraysh deniers of the Judgement; the general address expresses disgust at their attitude.
rows.anchor: Although the general word

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inner self provides evidence for resurrection, though deniers think decayed bones cannot be gathered; God will restore them in perfect detail, including finger joints.
rows.anchor: These verses assert that the evidence on the Day of Judgement is found within man; one does not have to look in the external world.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bunān means each section of a finger, so restoring them implies that God can rejoin even the smallest joints.
rows.anchor: each of “the sections of a finger”.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qādirīn is an accusative of state (ḥāl) linked to the plural pronoun in najmaʿa.
rows.anchor: an accusative of state ( hāl)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers' bones argument is empty; in reality, desire enslaves them and they want to sin before God's judge within them, like a thief before a judge.
rows.anchor: The reality is that they have become slaves

rows.speaker: Exegetes
rows.claim: Exegetes generally read “before him” as man's wish to keep sinning in the future life, which leads him to invent excuses for denying the Judgement.
rows.anchor: Exegetes have generally taken the word

rows.claim: Islahi rejects the future-life reading because it neither connects the phrase to the reproaching soul nor makes the verse an irrefutable argument against denial.
rows.anchor: nor does it become an irrefutable argument

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Before him” means before his conscience and reproaching soul: he persists in wrongdoing despite that faculty's warnings.
rows.anchor: Here the word “in front of” means

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conscience is sufficient evidence for the Judgement, though no one can stop a person brazen enough to lie to his own conscience.
rows.anchor: The argument found in this verse is that

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since conscience is a judge appointed by God, committing vice against it is effectively committing vice in God's presence.
rows.anchor: a vice committed before it is a vice committed before God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse depicts the deniers' stubbornness: despite their awareness of an inner court, they sarcastically ask when the Judgement will come and demand proof before believing.
rows.anchor: This is a mention of the stubbornness

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their taunt is that the threatened Day should already have come, and that they will not be convinced by words alone.
rows.anchor: If it is to come why is it not coming? We are tired of being threatened about it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though they act ready now, the deniers will be terrorized by the horrors and ask where to flee.
rows.anchor: But where will they run to when

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because demanding to see the Day is absurd, the Qur’an answers by portraying some of its horrors instead.
rows.anchor: some horrific aspects of that Day are portrayed by it in these verses.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The upheaval is mutashābihāt whose true form cannot be grasped here; the sun and moon leave their orbits and follow one path to depict the terror and prompt people to seek guidance.
rows.anchor: We cannot grasp their true form in this world.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Later sūrahs in this group portray other aspects of the Judgement, but they too offer only a small portion of what will happen, beyond what language can fully describe.
rows.anchor: various other aspects of the Day will be depicted.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer to “Whither to flee?” is that every path closes except refuge with God; towards Him is the destination that Day.
rows.anchor: Except for seeking refuge with God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgement reveals the consequences of deeds, including evil committed and good left undone; the heedless will regret their failures, rejecting messengers, and lack of faith.
rows.anchor: the real reason for the advent of the Day of Judgement.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The terms qadam and akhkhar encompass all evil deeds and vices people committed.
rows.anchor: embrace all the evil deeds and vices committed by such people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Success in the Hereafter requires good deeds and avoidance of evil; those indifferent to or denying it neglect success and persist in deeds leading to doom, so the verse warns them.
rows.anchor: such deprived and bereft people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the passage digresses to the deniers' question and the Judgement's portrayal, it returns to the original discussion of conscience and completes it.
rows.anchor: the subject under discussion is completed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A witness upon his own self” means each person testifies against himself; the reproaching soul within him bears witness to the Hereafter.
